children.text: Use h=\(6.626\times10^{-34}\) J s, ħ=h/(2π), c=\(2.998\times10^{8}\) m/s, electron mass me=\(9.109\times10^{-31}\) kg, e=\(1.602\times10^{-19}\) C, ε0=\(8.854\times10^{-12}\) F/m, kB=\(1.381\times10^{-23}\) J/K and atomic mass unit u=\(1.661\times10^{-27}\) kg. A quantum particle in a one-dimensional infinite well has V=0 for 0≤x≤L and infinite V outside. Its de Broglie standing wave has nodes at both walls. Photon transitions conserve energy. Later parts use the specified simple molecular, gas and optical-lattice models. The standing-wave condition is \(2L=n\lambda_{dB}\), with \(p=h/\lambda_{dB}\).
Find the smallest positive energy in the box.
Find the wavelength emitted in the transition E2→E1.

nodes.alt: Original Cy5 chemical structure, conjugated backbone with mean spacing l and effective 10.5 l potential well.

children.text: The Cy5 backbone contributes ten noninteracting electrons to a well of length L=10.5ℓ, where ℓ=140 pm. Include Pauli exclusion and spin. Find the longest absorbed wavelength from the electronic ground state, in terms of ℓ and constants, and numerically.
Cy3 has two fewer carbon atoms, eight mobile electrons and a well shorter by 2ℓ. Determine the direction and magnitude of the shift relative to Cy5.
Use dimensions to express the positive spontaneous decay rate K in ε0,h, wavelength λ and transition dipole moment d. The dimensionless prefactor is 16π³/3.
For d≈2.4eℓ and the Cy5 wavelength, estimate τ=1/K.
For a noninteracting gas of 87Rb atoms in thermal equilibrium, estimate typical momentum and de Broglie wavelength from rms speed.
Estimate spacing ℓ in a gas of number density n. Setting it equal to the rms de Broglie wavelength, find critical temperature Tc.
At Tc=100 nK compute nc for mass m=87u. Compare with n0 at 300 K and \(10^{5}\) Pa by giving n0 and n0/nc.

nodes.alt: Original three interfering laser directions, two sets of hexagonal symmetry axes and an example saddle surface.

children.text: Three equal-amplitude plane waves of wavenumber k, frequency ω and z polarization travel in the xy plane at 120° intervals. Choose k1=k(1,0), k2=k(−1/2,√3/2), k3=k(−1/2,−√3/2). Each field is E0 cos(ki·r−ωt). For V=−α〈E²〉, α>0, find V as a constant plus three cosines and identify their vectors.
Prove invariance under rotations by 60° around the origin.
Find VX(x)=V(x,0), VY(y)=V(0,y) and one representative of each periodically repeated minimum and maximum of these one-variable functions.
Eliminate saddle points and identify the six true minima nearest to the origin. Express lattice spacing a in laser wavelength λlas.

Estimate the principal quantum number n for a Rb Rydberg electron with classical circular radius equal to λlas=380 nm. Use angular momentum nħ and one effective positive elementary core charge. Give formula and number.

children.text: The longest standing-wave wavelength is 2L, giving p=h/(2L) and \(E_{min}=h^2/(8mL^2)\).
Fit n half-wavelengths into L: λn=2L/n. Thus \(E_n=h^2n^2/(8mL^2)\).

Two opposite-spin electrons fit each spatial level, filling n=1 to 5. The smallest allowed excitation is 5→6, giving \[\lambda=\frac{8m_ec(10.5\ell)^2}{11h}=\frac{882m_ec\ell^2}{11h}\simeq647\,\mathrm{nm}.\]

Cy3 fills four levels and absorbs in the 4→5 transition. With L=8.5ℓ, \(\lambda_{Cy3}=8m_ec(8.5\ell)^2/(9h)\simeq518\,\mathrm{nm}\). The absorption edge shifts about 129 nm towards blue. The electron count must change along with box length.

The dimensions force \(K\propto\epsilon_0^{-1}h^{-1}\lambda^{-3}d^2\). Thus \[K=\frac{16\pi^3d^2}{3\epsilon_0h\lambda^3}.\] As a positive decay rate, K satisfies dN/dt=−KN. The source's unsigned definition omits that minus sign.
Use the Cy5 emission/absorption-edge wavelength in the rate expression. \(\tau=3\epsilon_0h\lambda^3/[16\pi^3(2.4e\ell)^2]\simeq3.3\,\mathrm{ns}\).
The volume per atom gives ℓ=n^(−1/3). Equating wavelengths gives \(T_c=h^2n^{2/3}/(3mk_B)\). This is the problem's estimate, not the exact ideal-Bose-gas transition coefficient.

\(n_c=(3mk_BT_c)^{3/2}/h^3\simeq1.59\times10^{18}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\). The ideal gas law gives \(n_0=p_0/(k_BT_0)\simeq2.41\times10^{25}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\). The ordinary gas is about \(1.5\times10^{7}\) times denser.

Use 〈cos a cos b〉=cos(a−b)/2. Then \[V=-\alpha E_0^2[3/2+\cos(\mathbf b_1\cdot\mathbf r)+\cos(\mathbf b_2\cdot\mathbf r)+\cos(\mathbf b_3\cdot\mathbf r)],\] with b1=k2−k3=k(0,√3), b2=k3−k1=k(−3/2,−√3/2), b3=k1−k2=k(3/2,−√3/2).
A 60° rotation permutes the set of six reciprocal vectors ±b1,±b2,±b3. Since cosine is even, changing a vector to its negative does not alter its term. The sum and hence V are invariant.

\[V_X=-\alpha E_0^2[5/2+2\cos(3kx/2)],\quad V_Y=-\alpha E_0^2[3/2+\cos2\phi+2\cos\phi],\quad\phi=\sqrt3ky/2.\] VX has minima at x=0 and maxima at x=2π/(3k), modulo 4π/(3k). For VY, solve sin2φ+sinφ=0. In 0≤φ<2π, minima occur at φ=0 (deep) and π (shallow), maxima at 2π/3 and 4π/3. The φ=π minimum is only a one-dimensional minimum.

The point x=0, φ=π is a minimum along y but a maximum along x, so is a saddle. The nearest true minima are \((a,0),(a/2,\sqrt3a/2),(-a/2,\sqrt3a/2),(-a,0),(-a/2,-\sqrt3a/2),(a/2,-\sqrt3a/2)\). Here \(a=4\pi/(3k)=2\lambda_{las}/3\).
Equate Coulomb and centripetal forces and impose merv=nħ. Then \(r=4\pi\epsilon_0n^2\hbar^2/(m_ee^2)\), so \[n=\frac e\hbar\sqrt{\frac{m_e\lambda_{las}}{4\pi\epsilon_0}}\simeq85.\]

solution.text:
Particles and Waves
a.1. Ground-state energy
The longest standing-wave wavelength is 2L, giving p=h/(2L) and \(E_{min}=h^2/(8mL^2)\).
a.2. All box levels
Fit n half-wavelengths into L: λn=2L/n. Thus \(E_n=h^2n^2/(8mL^2)\).
a.3. First emission wavelength
The photon energy is \(3h^2/(8mL^2)\). Therefore \(\lambda_{21}=hc/(E_2-E_1)=8mcL^2/(3h)\).
b.1. Cy5 absorption edge
Two opposite-spin electrons fit each spatial level, filling n=1 to 5. The smallest allowed excitation is 5→6, giving \[\lambda=\frac{8m_ec(10.5\ell)^2}{11h}=\frac{882m_ec\ell^2}{11h}\simeq647\,\mathrm{nm}.\]
b.2. Cy3 spectral shift
Cy3 fills four levels and absorbs in the 4→5 transition. With L=8.5ℓ, \(\lambda_{Cy3}=8m_ec(8.5\ell)^2/(9h)\simeq518\,\mathrm{nm}\). The absorption edge shifts about 129 nm towards blue. The electron count must change along with box length.
b.3. Spontaneous emission rate
The dimensions force \(K\propto\epsilon_0^{-1}h^{-1}\lambda^{-3}d^2\). Thus \[K=\frac{16\pi^3d^2}{3\epsilon_0h\lambda^3}.\] As a positive decay rate, K satisfies dN/dt=−KN. The source's unsigned definition omits that minus sign.
b.4. Cy5 lifetime
Use the Cy5 emission/absorption-edge wavelength in the rate expression. \(\tau=3\epsilon_0h\lambda^3/[16\pi^3(2.4e\ell)^2]\simeq3.3\,\mathrm{ns}\).
c.1. Thermal momentum and wavelength
Equipartition gives p²/(2m)=3kBT/2. Hence \(p=\sqrt{3mk_BT}\), \(\lambda_{dB}=h/\sqrt{3mk_BT}\).
c.2. Condensation estimate
The volume per atom gives ℓ=n^(−1/3). Equating wavelengths gives \(T_c=h^2n^{2/3}/(3mk_B)\). This is the problem's estimate, not the exact ideal-Bose-gas transition coefficient.
c.3. Critical density and comparison
\(n_c=(3mk_BT_c)^{3/2}/h^3\simeq1.59\times10^{18}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\). The ideal gas law gives \(n_0=p_0/(k_BT_0)\simeq2.41\times10^{25}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\). The ordinary gas is about \(1.5\times10^{7}\) times denser.
d.1. Three-beam lattice potential
Use 〈cos a cos b〉=cos(a−b)/2. Then \[V=-\alpha E_0^2[3/2+\cos(\mathbf b_1\cdot\mathbf r)+\cos(\mathbf b_2\cdot\mathbf r)+\cos(\mathbf b_3\cdot\mathbf r)],\] with b1=k2−k3=k(0,√3), b2=k3−k1=k(−3/2,−√3/2), b3=k1−k2=k(3/2,−√3/2).
d.2. Sixfold symmetry
A 60° rotation permutes the set of six reciprocal vectors ±b1,±b2,±b3. Since cosine is even, changing a vector to its negative does not alter its term. The sum and hence V are invariant.
d.3. Axis profiles and extrema
\[V_X=-\alpha E_0^2[5/2+2\cos(3kx/2)],\quad V_Y=-\alpha E_0^2[3/2+\cos2\phi+2\cos\phi],\quad\phi=\sqrt3ky/2.\] VX has minima at x=0 and maxima at x=2π/(3k), modulo 4π/(3k). For VY, solve sin2φ+sinφ=0. In 0≤φ<2π, minima occur at φ=0 (deep) and π (shallow), maxima at 2π/3 and 4π/3. The φ=π minimum is only a one-dimensional minimum.
d.4. True lattice minima
The point x=0, φ=π is a minimum along y but a maximum along x, so is a saddle. The nearest true minima are \((a,0),(a/2,\sqrt3a/2),(-a/2,\sqrt3a/2),(-a,0),(-a/2,-\sqrt3a/2),(a/2,-\sqrt3a/2)\). Here \(a=4\pi/(3k)=2\lambda_{las}/3\).
d.5. Rydberg quantum number
Equate Coulomb and centripetal forces and impose merv=nħ. Then \(r=4\pi\epsilon_0n^2\hbar^2/(m_ee^2)\), so \[n=\frac e\hbar\sqrt{\frac{m_e\lambda_{las}}{4\pi\epsilon_0}}\simeq85.\]
